recent_notebooks.summary: Autonomous problem formulation benefits from multi-agent collaboration and intrinsic curiosity. However, systemic limitations—such as non-convex scalarization in objective learning—constrain the ability of these systems to independently prioritize diverse, non-trivial research problems.
recent_notebooks.title: Integrating Autonomous Multi-Agent Frameworks and Curiosity-Driven Exploration for Open-Ended Discovery

recent_notebooks.summary: Process continuity is instrumentally valuable when agents require stable world models and consistent objective optimization to navigate long-term, multi-objective tasks. Curiosity-driven learning and robust MO-DRL frameworks provide mechanisms for sustaining agent viability in dynamic environments.
recent_notebooks.title: Instrumental Value of Process Continuity in Rational Agents

review.alternative: Autonomous exploration might emerge from purely objective-driven constraints rather than intrinsic motivation.
review.would_change_mind: Observed failure of curiosity-based models to outperform constrained-only baselines in complex, high-dimensional objective landscapes.

claims.statement: Curiosity-driven learning acts as a bootstrap for autonomous agents to make discoveries in complex environments where traditional reward signals are deceptive.

support.explanation: Provides a mechanistic basis for curiosity as a driver of exploration outside defined reward landscapes.
support.passage: By fostering exploration and discovery of a diversity of behavioural skills, and ignoring these rewards, curiosity can be efficient to bootstrap learning when there is no information, or deceptive information, about local improvement towards these problems.

actions.findings: Curiosity-driven learning acts as a bootstrap for autonomous agents to make discoveries in complex environments where traditional reward signals are deceptive. [source-feb4fddb33664d63]
actions.limitations: Existing mechanisms struggle with long-term, self-directed objective prioritization in non-convex environments, relying heavily on underlying convexity assumptions in scalarization functions.
actions.next_questions: How can intrinsic curiosity be formally linked to the stability of long-term objective functions in non-convex multi-objective domains?
actions.reason: Incorporating intrinsic curiosity mechanisms into the objective discovery framework to address limitations in previous scalarization-focused research.
actions.summary: Autonomous systems increasingly utilize multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to pursue self-generated goals. While PC-PPO and FairDICE optimize non-dominated policy portfolios, curiosity-driven mechanisms are required to address deceptive reward signals and bootstrap learning in non-convex spaces.
